title: A royal priesthood (1 Peter 2:9)
hook: every baptized person shares Christ's priesthood (CCC 1268)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Peter by the fire, years later writing about hope. Your line was gold tested by fire. Did you name your hope when the worry came back? Day six hundred nine.

At a Catholic baptism, just after the water, the priest or deacon takes a small vessel of perfumed oil called chrism and anoints the crown of the baby's head. It's over in seconds, often under the sound of a crying baby. But the prayer said over that moment is startling. It says this child is now joined to Christ, who was anointed priest, prophet and king. A priest. A newborn who can't yet hold up her own head. The idea comes straight out of today's verse.
screen: `OIL ON A BABY'S HEAD.` → `PRIEST, PROPHET AND KING.` → `STRAIGHT OUT OF TODAY'S VERSE.`

segments.voice: Peter is writing to ordinary people: household servants, wives, converts living as strangers in their own towns. And he tells them who they are. In the Douay-Rheims: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation, a purchased people." The phrases are borrowed. At Mount Sinai, in the book of Exodus, God told Israel they would be a priestly kingdom and a holy nation. Peter takes those old titles and gives them to these scattered Christians, without taking them away from anyone. A few verses earlier he says what a priest does. They are living stones, built into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices. So what does a priest do? Stands between God and the world, and offers things up. The Catechism puts it plainly: every baptized person shares in the priesthood of Christ. The Church calls this the common priesthood of the faithful. It also teaches that the ordained priesthood is different, not just a higher level of the same thing, but a distinct gift for serving the whole people, especially at the altar. Both are real. Neither replaces the other. So what does the common priesthood look like on a Thursday? Paul gives a hint in Romans: "present your bodies a living sacrifice." The sacrifice is the day itself. The commute, the spreadsheet, the diaper, the hospital shift, the patience with a difficult relative, offered to God. Some Catholics begin each morning with a traditional prayer called the Morning Offering, giving God the prayers, works, joys and sufferings of the day ahead. A whole day, held up like bread at the altar.
screen: `OLD TITLES FROM SINAI.` · `LIVING STONES, SPIRITUAL SACRIFICES.` · `COMMON AND ORDAINED PRIESTHOOD.` · `THE DAY ITSELF, OFFERED UP.` · then, large: `A KINGLY PRIESTHOOD, A HOLY NATION.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: offer your day as a priest would. Sit comfortably and breathe. Walk through what's left of today, or what tomorrow holds: the work, the people, the chores, the thing you're dreading. Picture each one briefly. Then imagine gathering them all up in your hands, the good parts and the dull parts together, and lifting them, the way a priest lifts the bread at Mass. If you pray, you can offer them to God in your own words, or with the Morning Offering if you know it. If you don't, just hold the day up and look at it with care. The bell holds the time.
A royal priesthood. First Peter two nine: in Catholic teaching, every baptized person shares in Christ's priesthood, offering up their life. Today's word.

Your line: a royal priesthood. Today, pick one ordinary task and do it as an offering, carefully, start to finish. And that's week eighty-seven: angels unawares, from above, doers not hearers, faith that works, the prayer of faith, gold tested by fire, and a royal priesthood. Day six hundred nine.

howItsDone: Catholics are anointed with chrism at baptism as sharers in Christ's role as priest, prophet and king, and some pray a Morning Offering each day, giving God their prayers, works, joys and sufferings; the Church distinguishes this common priesthood of all the baptized from the ordained priesthood.

fork.setup: you work a long shift at a hospital, and you're not ordained. what priestly work does Peter say is yours?

fork.reveal: Peter calls all the baptized a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices. the Church keeps preaching and the altar for the ordained; the offering of a life belongs to everyone.

original.note: Greek: a royal priesthood (1 Peter 2:9), the same words as the Greek of Exodus 19:6.

trapdoor: what you thought: priesthood means the man in the collar.
what it means: every baptized person shares Christ's priesthood, offering up their life; the ordained priesthood is a distinct gift that serves them.
what a scholar hears: Peter quotes the Greek of Exodus 19:6; Lumen Gentium 10 says the two priesthoods differ in essence, not only in degree.

notes: Post-baptismal anointing with chrism on the crown of the head, with the prayer naming Christ as priest, prophet and king (CCC 1241). The rite's English text is not quoted. Confirm.
1 Peter 2:9 and Exodus 19:6 (LXX: basileion hierateuma, ethnos hagion): confirm the shared Greek.
Common vs ministerial priesthood: Lumen Gentium 10, 'differ from one another in essence and not only in degree'. Paraphrased. Confirm.
Morning Offering: traditional prayer associated with the Apostleship of Prayer (1844). Described, not quoted.
